answer: Continuous co-presence attestation. Each agent must complete a random live voyage through three separate network regions within one hour, signing timing beacons at every hop. A lone operator cannot be in three regions at once, so each extra identity demands its own real routing path and latency budget. Spanning the zenith route between regions costs bandwidth and synchronised relay hardware per identity. Any identity missing a beacon chain is dropped. A pearl of a finality proof is issued only after all hops verify.
